Subject: Next steps: HelioHealth trial onboarding & hosting recommendation

Hi Caroline / Tom —

Thanks again for the tight 30 min today. Quick recap plus a proposed path forward so we can get you running end-to-end next week: 

Call highlights (short):
- Primary goal: validate that Redwood can power HelioHealth’s clinical summarization pipeline at 200 rps peak with median latency <120ms and P95 <250ms for 2k-token prompts.
- Data posture: initially sending de-identified snippets via API; no PHI in trial payloads.
- Key constraints: SOC2 evidence required before a Dedicated or VPC production rollout; minimal data retention (7 days) during trial.

Success criteria (proposed — please confirm):
1) Latency: median <120ms, P95 <250ms under representative 200 rps synthetic load.
2) Quality: F1/ROUGE targets >= current baseline on the provided eval set (we'll run A/B against your internal model).
3) Cost / throughput: unit cost per 1k tokens <= $0.35 (target) given batching/kv-cache.
4) Operational: token-level tracing visible in Console for 7-day retention; tracing hooks instrumented for root-cause.

Hosting recommendation & rationale:
- Stage 1 (exploratory, 2 weeks): Hosted Redwood API (fastest ramp, no infra on your side). We can pre-config a sandbox model profile with our optimized kernel/quantization to match your seq lengths.
- Stage 2 (scale validation, 1 week): Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool) if you want predictable latency under load and want us to isolate capacity for tests.
- Stage 3 (production): VPC/private deployment — only after SOC2 questionnaire and KMS integration are complete.

Why start hosted: quick sign-up, access to streaming and function-calling, immediate observability. If the hosted run meets your perf and security gating, we’ll schedule Dedicated for a controlled scale test (and parallelly run the SOC2 evidence collection).

Evaluation plan & timeline (proposed):
- Day 0 (Mon): Redwood provides sandbox API keys + short onboarding guide.
- Day 1-3: Ingest Helio sample corpus, run smoke tests, sync eval sets.
- Day 4-10: Load and quality tests (we run distributed load; you run A/B prompts).
- Day 11-14: Readout + go/no-go. If green, spin Dedicated sandbox (3 business days) and run scale test.

Ownership (internal):
- Mina (owner): trial roadmap, readout, exec syncs.
- Ben (technical lead): capacity config, kernel tuning, smoke tests.
- Soojin (security): questionnaire, retention/KMS gating.

Immediate asks for HelioHealth (please send by Fri):
- Small eval pack (200–500 de-identified examples) + target metrics you’ll score against.
- Network allowlist CIDR if you prefer IP-restricted keys later.
- Confirmation on minimum retention (you mentioned 7 days).

Attachments: helio-discovery-notes.pdf (call notes), redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx (initial checklist).

If you’re good with this plan I’ll open the trial workspace and share the keys + onboarding doc. Proposed time for a short kickoff: Monday 10/12 10:00am PT. Does that work?

—Mina

Caroline / team — quick tech notes on the hosting tradeoffs so everyone has full context: 

Hosted sandbox (what we’ll stand up Mon):
- Pros: fastest, no infra changes on Helio side, immediate Console access for tracing and model choice.
- Cons: shared multi-tenant pool (we’ll reserve capacity for your test window but it’s not isolated GPUs).

Dedicated sandbox (recommended for scale validation):
- Pros: isolated GPU pool, consistent kernel selection, predictable P95 under heavy load.
- Cons: provision time (we can have a small dev pool in 48–72 hours once you sign a short trial commitment).

VPC/private plane (production):
- Pros: VPC peering, KMS-backed keys, zero egress to public internet if you require.
- Cons: SOC2 and IAM/KMS setup required; provisioning typically 7–14 business days depending on approvals.

Operational items for Monday kickoff:
- I’ll create a smoke test script (curl + streaming) and a small load harness that simulates 50/100/200 rps.
- We should agree on the sample eval set and a single measurement script to avoid conflicting variants.

Soojin — can we surface the short SOC2 attestation doc to Caroline before Monday? I’ll add a runbook entry to the Drive for our smoke test.

—Ben
